about: Post-quantum cryptography readiness of this estate, assessed against what the estate demonstrably does. Based on the NIST post-quantum standards (FIPS 203 ML-KEM, FIPS 204 ML-DSA, FIPS 205 SLH-DSA), NIST's draft transition plan (IR 8547) and the scope the RBI has given its Q-SAFE committee (cryptography inventory / CBOM, crypto-agility, most-exposed systems). Not a regulator's checklist: RBI has not issued quantum requirements yet.

source.title: Post-quantum cryptography: NIST FIPS 203/204/205, NIST IR 8547 (draft) and the RBI Q-SAFE committee
source.issued: FIPS 203/204/205 final 13 Aug 2024; HQC selected as a backup KEM Mar 2025; IR 8547 initial public draft Nov 2024; RBI Q-SAFE committee press release 25 May 2026
source.caveat: The FIPS dates are NIST's. IR 8547 (deprecate RSA/ECC after 2030, disallow after 2035) and FIPS 206 (FN-DSA) status come from secondary sources and are DRAFTS: verify at csrc.nist.gov. The RBI committee had not reported when this was written; nothing here is an RBI requirement. Status is our own judgement.

items.title: Cryptography inventory / CBOM of the estate
items.note: `./securax crypto` reads the actual certificates, TLS configuration, verifier source and backups and ranks what to fix first; `--cbom` emits a CycloneDX 1.6 Cryptography Bill of Materials. Scope is this estate only: the entity's wider estate is theirs.

items.title: Hybrid post-quantum key exchange for traffic that leaves the machine (ML-KEM-768 + X25519, FIPS 203)
items.note: The HTTPS edge offers X25519MLKEM768 first and keeps classical curves for clients that lack it; the tls_edge journey negotiates the hybrid group against the real edge (OpenSSL 3.5 client) and proves a classical-only client still connects. Browsers that support it (current Chrome, Edge, Firefox) get it automatically.

items.title: Hybrid key exchange on the internal service-to-service hops
items.note: The sidecars use the same nginx build and group list, but the negotiated group is proven only at the edge. These hops never leave the machine, so harvest-now-decrypt-later is not the risk there.
items.next: Assert the negotiated group on a sidecar in the tls_internal journey.

items.title: Post-quantum signatures / certificates (ML-DSA, FIPS 204)
items.note: Certificates and the private CA are ECDSA P-256. A signature is forgeable only while the algorithm is broken (never retroactively), and browsers and CA tooling do not yet accept ML-DSA certificates, so this follows rather than leads.
items.next: Issue a hybrid or ML-DSA estate CA once OpenSSL tooling and browsers accept it; keep the algorithm a single setting in governance/tls.py.

items.title: CA lifetime does not outlive the NIST draft disallow date (2035)
items.note: The estate CA is valid for 10 years, so it expires after 2035, the date NIST's draft proposes for disallowing P-256. `./securax crypto` flags it from the certificate itself; the CA is private, so the reissue date is ours to choose.
items.next: Shorten the CA validity or schedule its reissue before 2035; track in the rhythm.

items.title: Crypto-agility of caller authentication (JWT / OIDC)
items.note: The gateway verifier accepts RS256 (RSA, quantum-vulnerable for signatures) and HS256 (HMAC-SHA-256, quantum-safe with a long secret) and only the algorithms the operator allows. There is no ES256/EdDSA path and no ML-DSA path yet, so moving needs a verifier addition, not just a setting.
items.next: Add ES256 and EdDSA; add ML-DSA when identity providers issue it. Prefer HS256 with a 256-bit secret for service tokens meanwhile.

items.title: Symmetric encryption and hashing sized for a quantum adversary
items.note: TLS bulk encryption is AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305 (AES-256 and ChaCha20 stay strong under Grover; AES-128 is offered for compatibility and is the first to retire); API keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes.

items.title: Backups encrypted at rest with a quantum-safe construction
items.note: OpenPGP symmetric AES-256 with a key file you keep off the machine or a typed passphrase; there is no public-key step to break. A wrong key and a tampered file are refused before anything is touched; `crypto --strict` fails while backups are unprotected. Strength equals the strength of your key file / passphrase. Integrity is OpenPGP's modification-detection code.

items.title: Key exchange on calls to cloud AI providers
items.note: The router image that makes the calls offers hybrid key exchange (OpenSSL 3.5 or later, probed by `crypto`), but the provider decides what is accepted. Sensitive classes stay local by the data-tier router, so only what you accepted to send to a cloud travels.
items.next: Re-run `./securax crypto` after each router image update; record which providers negotiate the hybrid group.

items.title: Data with long confidentiality horizons is identified and kept off recordable paths
items.note: Classification-aware routing keeps RED data local and the residency guard restricts regions. Nothing yet labels data by how long it must stay secret.
items.next: Add a retention-horizon label to the data classes and let `crypto` list which classes cross an unprotected path.

items.title: Remote-access tunnel with a post-quantum handshake
items.note: Tailscale / WireGuard use Curve25519; a standard post-quantum WireGuard handshake does not exist yet (a pre-shared key mixed into the handshake is the interim mitigation). The estate does not run the VPN.
items.next: Document the pre-shared-key option and keep sensitive traffic on the local network.

items.title: FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules
items.note: The estate uses the OpenSSL builds inside its images without the FIPS provider enabled.
items.next: Document which images would need a FIPS provider and whether a validated build exists for them.

items.title: Release provenance signatures
items.note: SLSA attestations use Sigstore keyless signing (ECDSA P-256): quantum-vulnerable for signatures, third-party controlled, and not retroactively forgeable.
items.next: Follow Sigstore's post-quantum signature work; nothing to change here.

items.title: Quantum-migration plan, owner and timeline; board reporting
items.note: A plan, an accountable owner and a timeline belong to the regulated entity. `./securax crypto` supplies the inventory and the ranked do-first list as an input.

items.title: Vendor and cloud-provider post-quantum roadmaps (concentration and third-party risk)
items.note: Asking each provider and vendor for its post-quantum roadmap and contract position is the entity's process.

items.title: Key custody for the entity's own keys (HSM / KMS, rotation)
items.note: The estate holds its own CA key and the backup key file; the entity's HSM/KMS and key-ceremony controls are the entity's.

items.title: RBI quantum-safe requirements
items.note: The RBI constituted the Q-SAFE committee on 25 May 2026 (cryptography inventory / CBOM, crypto-agility, most-exposed systems, vendor tool maturity, a roadmap); its report was pending when this was written. No requirement exists yet to map to. Review this map when it is published.
